s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic ulcerative skin lesion with hyperkeratotic edges and unstructured whitish areas
salient_findings: Painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space of the right foot
Verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges
Unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis on dermoscopy
key_facts: 60-year-old patient with no significant medical history
3-year history of macerated skin between the toes
18-month history of progressively enlarging ulcer
Received multiple antifungal regimens without improvement
Ulcer measures 3 cm in diameter and extends onto the dorsum of the foot
Hyperkeratotic edges and whitish, fissured base
Dermoscopy reveals unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis
No palpable popliteal and inguinal lymph nodes

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic ulcerative skin lesion with hyperkeratotic edges

shortlist.label: Verrucous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Verrucous, infected ulceration with hyperkeratotic edges

shortlist.label: Chronic pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Progressively enlarging ulcer with unstructured whitish areas

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic skin lesion with hyperkeratotic edges and whitish base

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base, along with dermoscopy revealing unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis, is consistent with verrucous carcinoma. The lack of response to antifungal treatment and the progressive enlargement of the ulcer also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the specific description of the ulcer as verrucous and the dermoscopy findings are more characteristic of verrucous carcinoma.

rejected.label: Chronic pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: Typically presents with painful ulcers but lacks the verrucous and hyperkeratotic features described in this case.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Usually presents as a solitary, rapidly growing nodule that can resemble a verrucous carcinoma but often has a more rapid growth phase and can spontaneously resolve.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Less likely given the location and description of the ulcer, as basal cell carcinoma typically presents as a slow-growing, well-defined nodule or ulcer on sun-exposed areas.
